title: Getting ready for university
paragraphs: You’ve studied hard, you’ve got the grades and now you’re off to university! This is the journey that many students are taking, but how prepared are they to leave home, stand on their own two feet and be self-sufficient? One study, carried out by the Higher Education Policy Institute and Unite Students in 2017, suggested that as well as being excited and nervous, many students are deeply ill-informed about what to expect.

Of course, flying the nest to go to university is the opportunity of a lifetime, but to make the most of it needs some preparation before you arrive. This means learning life skills such as cooking and cleaning. You’ll no longer be able to rely on Mum and Dad to feed you or clear up after you, so try to learn how to make some staple dishes that are quick and easy to prepare. Graduate Peter Rogers told the BBC: “I didn’t really have anything other than rudimentary cookery skills before I went to university and found learning to cook was reasonably enjoyable.” Other things to do while at home is to practise some of those household chores, like operating the washing machine or ironing your clothes!

These domestic skills will come in useful because students will probably be living with others such as in a flat share or shared campus-based accommodation. This will also require taking responsibility for managing their finances because, apart from tuition fees, accommodation is likely to be the biggest cost for students living away from home. However, the Higher Education Policy Institute and Unite Students study found only about half of the would-be students surveyed identified rent as the biggest expense and concluded that this suggests more should be done to help in the transition between school and university.

New students are going to have to be sociable as well – not just relying on old friends at home. Going to university requires meeting new people and making new friends. This often begins in Freshers’ Week although journalism student Emmeke Megannety warns that: “People starting uni need to remember that the people you meet in your first week will not necessarily be your friends for life.” But whatever your expectations, it’s good to be prepared for the time of your life.

vocabulary.entry: self-sufficient /ˌself səˈfɪʃnt/ adj. 自给自足的；能独立生活的
vocabulary.example: After a few months of living alone, she became more self-sufficient.
vocabulary.translation: 独自生活几个月后，她变得更加能自给自足了。

vocabulary.entry: ill-informed /ˌɪl ɪnˈfɔːmd/ adj. 所知甚少的；消息不灵通的
vocabulary.example: He made an ill-informed decision based on incomplete data.
vocabulary.translation: 他基于不完整的数据做出了一个考虑不周的决定。

vocabulary.entry: fly the nest /flaɪ ðə nest/ 离家独立生活
vocabulary.example: Many young people fly the nest when they go to college.
vocabulary.translation: 许多年轻人上大学时就离家独立生活了。

vocabulary.term: stand on one's own two feet
vocabulary.entry: stand on one's own two feet /stænd ɒn wʌnz əʊn tuː fiːt/ 独立自主
vocabulary.example: It's time for you to stand on your own two feet and make your own decisions.
vocabulary.translation: 你该学会独立自主，自己做决定了。

vocabulary.entry: opportunity of a lifetime /ˌɒpəˈtjuːnəti ɒv ˈlaɪftaɪm/ 一生难得的机遇
vocabulary.example: Winning the scholarship was an opportunity of a lifetime for her.
vocabulary.translation: 赢得这份奖学金对她来说是一生难得的机遇。

vocabulary.entry: make the most of /meɪk ðə məʊst ɒv/ 充分利用
vocabulary.example: You should make the most of the chance to study abroad.
vocabulary.translation: 你应该充分利用这次出国留学的机会。

vocabulary.entry: staple dish /ˈsteɪpl dɪʃ/ n. 家常菜；主食菜肴
vocabulary.example: Rice and stir-fried vegetables are staple dishes in many Asian households.
vocabulary.translation: 米饭和炒蔬菜是许多亚洲家庭的家常菜。

vocabulary.entry: rudimentary /ˌruːdɪˈmentri/ adj. 基础的；初步的
vocabulary.example: The course provides only rudimentary introduction to the subject.
vocabulary.translation: 这门课程只对该学科做了基础的介绍。

vocabulary.entry: cookery /ˈkʊkəri/ n. 烹饪术；烹饪
vocabulary.example: She attended a cookery class to learn how to bake bread.
vocabulary.translation: 她参加了一个烹饪班，学习如何烤面包。

vocabulary.entry: household chore /ˈhaʊshəʊld tʃɔː(r)/ n. 家务琐事
vocabulary.example: Washing dishes is one of the most common household chores.
vocabulary.translation: 洗碗是最常见的家务琐事之一。

vocabulary.entry: iron /ˈaɪən/ v. 熨烫（衣物）
vocabulary.example: She spent the afternoon ironing all her shirts.
vocabulary.translation: 她花了一个下午熨烫所有的衬衫。

vocabulary.entry: accommodation /əˌkɒməˈdeɪʃn/ n. 住处；住宿
vocabulary.example: The university provides cheap accommodation for first-year students.
vocabulary.translation: 这所大学为大一新生提供廉价的住宿。

vocabulary.entry: tuition fee /tjuˈɪʃn fiː/ n. 学费
vocabulary.example: Many students take out loans to pay their tuition fees.
vocabulary.translation: 许多学生贷款来支付学费。

vocabulary.entry: finance /ˈfaɪnæns/ n. 财务状况；资金
vocabulary.example: He needs to improve his management of personal finance.
vocabulary.translation: 他需要改进对个人财务的管理。

vocabulary.entry: expense /ɪkˈspens/ n. 开销；花费
vocabulary.example: Accommodation is our biggest expense when travelling abroad.
vocabulary.translation: 出国旅行时，住宿费是我们最大的开销。

vocabulary.entry: would-be /ˈwʊd bi/ adj. 未来的；准的
vocabulary.example: The book offers advice to would-be entrepreneurs.
vocabulary.translation: 这本书为准创业者提供了建议。

vocabulary.entry: identify /aɪˈdentɪfaɪ/ v. 确认；认出
vocabulary.example: She was asked to identify the suspect from a lineup of photos.
vocabulary.translation: 她被要求从一排照片中辨认出嫌疑人。

vocabulary.entry: transition /trænˈzɪʃn/ n. 过渡；转变
vocabulary.example: The transition from school to work can be difficult for young people.
vocabulary.translation: 从学校到职场的转变对年轻人来说可能很难。

vocabulary.entry: sociable /ˈsəʊʃəbl/ adj. 好交际的；合群的
vocabulary.example: She is a sociable person who enjoys meeting new people.
vocabulary.translation: 她是个爱交际的人，喜欢结识新朋友。

vocabulary.entry: Freshers’ Week /ˈfreʃəz wiːk/ n. 新生周
vocabulary.example: Freshers’ Week is a great time to make new friends at university.
vocabulary.translation: 新生周是在大学里结交新朋友的好时机。

vocabulary.entry: flat share /flæt ʃeə(r)/ n. 合租公寓
vocabulary.example: He lives in a flat share with three other students.
vocabulary.translation: 他和另外三名学生合租一套公寓。

vocabulary.entry: campus-based /ˈkæmpəs beɪst/ adj. 基于校园的
vocabulary.example: The university offers campus-based accommodation for students.
vocabulary.translation: 这所大学为学生提供校内住宿。

vocabulary.entry: responsibility /rɪˌspɒnsəˈbɪləti/ n. 责任；职责
vocabulary.example: Taking care of your own health is your personal responsibility.
vocabulary.translation: 照顾好自己的健康是你个人的责任。

vocabulary.entry: rely on /rɪˈlaɪ ɒn/ 依赖；依靠
vocabulary.example: You can't always rely on your parents to solve your problems.
vocabulary.translation: 你不能总是依赖父母来解决你的问题。

vocabulary.entry: journalism /ˈdʒɜːnəlɪzəm/ n. 新闻业；新闻学
vocabulary.example: She studied journalism at university and now works for a newspaper.
vocabulary.translation: 她大学时学的是新闻学，现在在一家报社工作。

sentences.english: You’ve studied hard, you’ve got the grades and now you’re off to university!
sentences.chinese: 你努力学习，拿到了满意的成绩，如今即将踏入大学校园！

sentences.english: This is the journey that many students are taking, but how prepared are they to leave home, stand on their own two feet and be self-sufficient?
sentences.chinese: 这是许多学生都会踏上的旅程，但他们是否做好了离家的准备，能否真正独立生活、自给自足呢？

sentences.english: One study, carried out by the Higher Education Policy Institute and Unite Students in 2017, suggested that as well as being excited and nervous, many students are deeply ill-informed about what to expect.
sentences.chinese: 高等教育政策研究所与联合学生公寓在2017年开展的一项研究表明，许多学生在满怀期待与忐忑的同时，对于大学生活的实际情况也知之甚少。

sentences.english: Of course, flying the nest to go to university is the opportunity of a lifetime, but to make the most of it needs some preparation before you arrive.
sentences.chinese: 当然，离家上大学是一生难得的机遇，但要想充分利用这段时光，就需要在入学前做好一些准备。

sentences.english: This means learning life skills such as cooking and cleaning.
sentences.chinese: 这意味着要学习烹饪、打扫这类生活技能。

sentences.english: You’ll no longer be able to rely on Mum and Dad to feed you or clear up after you, so try to learn how to make some staple dishes that are quick and easy to prepare.
sentences.chinese: 你不能再依赖父母为你做饭、收拾残局了，所以不妨学着做几道简单快捷易上手的家常菜。

sentences.english: Graduate Peter Rogers told the BBC: “I didn’t really have anything other than rudimentary cookery skills before I went to university and found learning to cook was reasonably enjoyable.”
sentences.chinese: 毕业生彼得·罗杰斯在接受BBC采访时表示：“上大学前，我只掌握了一些最基础的烹饪技能，后来发现学着做饭其实还挺有意思的。”

sentences.english: Other things to do while at home is to practise some of those household chores, like operating the washing machine or ironing your clothes!
sentences.chinese: 在家时还可以练习一些家务，比如操作洗衣机、熨烫衣物等等！

sentences.english: These domestic skills will come in useful because students will probably be living with others such as in a flat share or shared campus-based accommodation.
sentences.chinese: 这些居家技能迟早会派上用场，因为学生很可能会和别人合租公寓，或是住进校内的集体宿舍。

sentences.english: This will also require taking responsibility for managing their finances because, apart from tuition fees, accommodation is likely to be the biggest cost for students living away from home.
sentences.chinese: 这也意味着学生需要承担起管理个人财务的责任，因为对于离家在外的学生来说，除了学费，住宿费很可能就是最大的开销。

sentences.english: However, the Higher Education Policy Institute and Unite Students study found only about half of the would-be students surveyed identified rent as the biggest expense and concluded that this suggests more should be done to help in the transition between school and university.
sentences.chinese: 但高等教育政策研究所与联合学生公寓的这项研究发现，在受访的准大学生中，只有约半数人认为房租是最大的支出。研究结论指出，这意味着需要采取更多措施，帮助学生顺利完成从中学到大学的过渡。

sentences.english: New students are going to have to be sociable as well – not just relying on old friends at home.
sentences.chinese: 新生还得学会社交——不能只依赖家乡的老朋友。

sentences.english: Going to university requires meeting new people and making new friends.
sentences.chinese: 上大学就意味着要结识陌生人，结交新朋友。

sentences.english: This often begins in Freshers’ Week although journalism student Emmeke Megannety warns that: “People starting uni need to remember that the people you meet in your first week will not necessarily be your friends for life.”
sentences.chinese: 这通常从新生周就开始了，不过新闻系学生埃梅克·梅加内蒂提醒道：“刚开始上大学的人要记住，你第一周遇到的人，未必会成为你一辈子的朋友。”

sentences.english: But whatever your expectations, it’s good to be prepared for the time of your life.
sentences.chinese: 但无论你对大学生活有着怎样的期待，做好充分准备，才能迎接这段人生中最美好的时光。
